confidence_notes: I ran three web searches. One found the RBA rate for 18 Nov 2026 (0.6720 USD per AUD) as reported on the RBA site. Two looked up Querétaro prices on crowdsourced cost-of-living sites, which give rough figures that don't always agree. Coffee and beer look fairly reliable: cappuccino is about $3.6 on two indexes and $2-3 in one travel guide, and a domestic draft beer is about $2.0-2.4. Inexpensive meals range widely, from about $4.6 to $9.75. I chose about $8, just under the $9.75 figure that includes a drink, because a sit-down meal at an ordinary restaurant usually costs more than a comida corrida set lunch at $4-6. Sources also disagree on a mid-range three-course meal for two, from about $28 to $64. I used about $45. I found no reliable current prices for a cocktail or a glass of wine. Those two figures are based on their usual relationship to beer prices in Mexican cities, about 2.5x for a cocktail and 2.3x for wine, and loosely checked against a bottle-of-wine figure of about MX$337. The four accommodation figures are general model estimates for a mid-sized colonial and business city with steady domestic tourism. I did not check any live listings or booking prices for them, so they are the least certain of the ten. The reference period is July 2026, but the price data comes from crowdsourced pages dated anywhere from mid-2025 to October 2026.
comparable_city_reasoning: Querétaro is a prosperous Bajío city with business travel and a colonial historic centre. For prices it compares with Guanajuato, San Miguel de Allende (minus its expat premium) and mid-range parts of Guadalajara. Restaurant prices sit near Mexico's national urban averages, and hotel prices are slightly higher because of business demand.
